question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says 'When the cast or sorted door refuses to create a ticket for a red, an unticketed trouble is raised instead', but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline requires 'each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds'. The ticket's implementation writes a trouble when the door refuses, not a ticket. The two record types (Coding Ticket vs. Trouble Ticket) cannot both be written in the same situation; only one occurs per refusal.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands. The trouble does not replace the ticket: when a door refuses the cast, no ticket CAN be written in that act, and the trouble is the permanent record that 9.4.2.3.7.5 was not met (Law 7). The red still owes its ticket; _clear_unticketed clears the trouble only when a later run tickets the red or it reads green. Added as a constraint on the ticket.
